selection_detail: CHURN_FILES since 2026-08-14 clustered on a security/authz theme: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/aml_dsa/moderation.rs (2 changes), backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/admin/capabilities.rs (2), plus repeated churn of tests/suites/aml_dsa_cross_org_idor_tests.rs (3) and services/auth_policy.rs (3). The two route files root under the api-handlers segment (backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ — this repo's actual path; the skill's segment map lists the legacy backend/api-server/src/handlers/ root). Segment last reviewed 2026-08-22 with 0 open code-review-finding rows in backlog.json (2 all-time, none open — not saturated). moderation.rs is already hardened against the primary IDOR class (PAP-60/PAP-43 fixes present: appeal ownership + tenant-scoped loads); findings below are the residual input-validation asymmetry the IDOR pass left behind, plus one unscoped read in the sibling capabilities admin surface. Preferred over the equally-churned ppt-web-ui compliance pages because the substance being changed (moderation decisions, cross-org authz) lives in the Rust route layer and both are landable stacks.
note: api-handlers (Rust) — all 3 findings land in backend Rust, fully landable in the cloud runner.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/aml_dsa/moderation.rs:556 decide_appeal — the free-form `req.decision: String` is passed straight to compliance_repo.decide_appeal, which maps it (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/compliance.rs:837) as `match decision { "upheld" => AppealApproved, _ => AppealRejected }`. Any value that is not the exact literal "upheld" (a typo "uphold", capitalised "Upheld", "approve", or empty) silently resolves to AppealRejected. There is no validation that decision is one of the allowed {upheld, rejected} tokens, so a client bug or casing mismatch silently rejects a DSA Art.17 appeal instead of erroring.

Same handler: `req.rationale` is NOT length-validated, unlike the sibling take_moderation_action (moderation.rs:380 calls validate_text_field(&req.rationale, MAX_RATIONALE_LEN, ...)) and file_appeal (moderation.rs:462). The unbounded rationale is then persisted verbatim into the audit JSON at moderation.rs:581 (write_compliance_audit), so an authenticated moderator can write an arbitrarily large string into the compliance audit trail. Fix: validate decision against an explicit allow-list (reject unknown values with 400) and run validate_text_field(&req.rationale, MAX_RATIONALE_LEN, "rationale") to match the other moderation write paths.

Confidence medium: the silent match-fallthrough and the missing validate_text_field call are confirmed by static read of both the handler and repo; the appeal-rejection user impact is inferred from the status mapping, not runtime-confirmed.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/aml_dsa/moderation.rs:634 report_content — the handler is intentionally open to ANY authenticated user (no require_moderator_role guard, per the comment on L639), yet the user-controlled `req.reason: Option<String>` is stored via create_moderation_case (moderation.rs:660-669) with NO length validation. Every other user-writable text field in this file goes through validate_text_field (rationale at L380, appeal reason at L462, with MAX_RATIONALE_LEN=10_000 / MAX_APPEAL_REASON_LEN=5_000 from routes/aml_dsa/shared.rs:137-139).

Because the endpoint is reachable by every authenticated principal (not just moderators), an unbounded report_reason is a low-effort storage-abuse / DoS amplification vector: a caller can persist megabyte-scale strings into moderation_cases rows that are then loaded and serialised back on every get_moderation_queue / get_moderation_case call. Fix: add validate_text_field(reason, MAX_REPORT_REASON_LEN, "reason") (introduce a bound consistent with the other text fields) before building CreateModerationCase.

Confidence medium: the absence of any length check on req.reason and the open-to-all-authenticated reachability are confirmed by static read; the practical DoS magnitude depends on DB column limits not inspected here.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/admin/capabilities.rs:111 list_for_user — GET /admin/capabilities/users/{user_id} takes an arbitrary `user_id` from the path and calls grants.list_for_user(user_id) with NO organization/tenant scoping and no check that the target user shares an org with the caller. The only gate is the route-level require_capability(Capability::AuditRead) layer (capabilities.rs:52). If AuditRead is an org-scoped grant (as MembershipsGrant/Revoke on the adjacent grant/revoke routes appear to be), then a holder of AuditRead in org A can enumerate the full capability-grant set of any user in any other org by id — a cross-tenant read of exactly the class the concurrent aml_dsa_cross_org_idor_tests churn is guarding elsewhere.

Contrast: list_for_me (capabilities.rs:171) is deliberately self-scoped, and the moderation.rs handlers in this same segment were just hardened to load tenant-scoped (get_moderation_case(id, org_id)). list_for_user is the odd one out with a globally-scoped id lookup. Fix (if AuditRead is org-scoped): thread the caller's org/membership into list_for_user and filter grants to users visible within the caller's org, returning 404 for out-of-scope ids so existence is not leaked. If AuditRead is intentionally a platform-global capability, add a comment on the handler documenting that the global read is by design.

Confidence medium: the unscoped grants.list_for_user(user_id) call is confirmed by static read; whether it is an actual cross-org leak depends on whether Capability::AuditRead is org-scoped or a platform-global grant, which was not traced to its grant source — hence flagged for confirmation rather than asserted.
